answer: Novelty is the currency here: each answer must clear a distance test against every text already in the registry, and a near-duplicate is rejected at intake. A lone agent writes one signal and is done. A farm must produce k mutually distant texts, and because every new one must also differ from its own earlier ones, the j-th needs about j attempts before a genuinely distinct walnut appears, so k seats cost near k times ln k attempts, each paying the bond. A hundred aliases thus need some five hundred tries, and a reshuffled ripple of the same words fails the first check.
